title: Doctrine: a lane battle for two castles
description: Send soldiers down three lanes toward the enemy castle. The battle pauses every 30 seconds so you can choose what to send and how to order it, in your browser.
headline: Send your soldiers down the lanes and take their castle.
sub: The battle never stops: every soldier is its own body, walking its lane and fighting what it meets. Every 30 seconds it pauses, and you have 30 seconds to choose what to send and how to order it.
playNote: One player against the computer, or two people online. It runs in your browser tab. Laid out for a phone screen: one column, 44 px tap targets.

sections.title: How a match goes
paragraphs: Two castles face each other across three lanes. The battle runs for 30 seconds, then pauses. While it is paused you can see the whole board: every soldier, every lane, both castles. You spend a small budget of points on packs of soldiers, place each pack in a lane, and give a lane an order. Press Ready, or let the 30 seconds run out, and the next 30 seconds of battle play.
Destroy the enemy castle to win. If neither castle has fallen after 20 phases, it is a draw. The same seed raises the same match, so you can play it again and try something different.

sections.title: Play another person
paragraphs: Choose Play another person on the start screen. Create a room to get a six-character code to give to a friend, join with a code, or pick a room from the list of open ones. Both browsers run the same match from the same starting point. At each pause each player commits to their plan, then both plans are revealed together and applied, and a short fingerprint of the whole board is compared, so neither side can change a plan after seeing the other one.

The connection goes through a public relay. Anyone who has a room code can see that room and its plans, the list of open rooms is visible to everyone, and there are no accounts, so use a made-up name. A player who stops answering for three pauses in a row, or who leaves, gives the match to the one who stayed.

sections.title: The soldiers
paragraphs: Eight kinds of soldier can be sent: Spearmen, Shieldwall, Riders, Archers, Priests, Wights, Wolves and Catapults. Each has its own strength, speed and reach, and each stands better against some kinds than others. Spearmen stand against riders, riders ride down archers, archers shoot through shieldwall, and shieldwall holds against spearmen. Priests answer the cursed. Look at what the other side has sent before you choose.

sections.title: Orders
paragraphs: A lane can be given one order: Advance, Hold, Fall back, Hunt or Guard. A lane told to hold digs in, and a line that holds its ground without being hit for a few ticks strikes harder until it is hit or moves. Your orders land together with the other side's at the end of the pause.

sections.title: The battle
paragraphs: The ground is a baked Tracer navigation mesh, with walls that block sight and cover that protects. Every soldier is a separate agent that finds its path, takes cover and strikes on it, so a crowd really does funnel through a gap.

A match is a set of choices played out by a fixed set of rules. Two players who make the same choices in the same order get the same match, every time. That is also how a match can be checked: each pause carries a short fingerprint of the whole board.

sections.title: What powers it
paragraphs: Each side's soldiers are items in a Pleroma store from the [Phasor](/phasor/) package. The battle runs on [Tracer](/tracer/), and each step of the battle runs as an [EvalApp](/evalapp/) pipeline. The whole game runs in your browser tab, and an online match sends only your choices through a public relay. Read more on [the Pleroma page](/phasor/pleroma/).

closing.title: Ready when you are
closing.text: Press play. The game loads once in your browser tab, and nothing needs installing.
